title: Singleton images of projective lines before and after scalar extension
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $L/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $X$ be any $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Let $r:\mathbf P^1_k\to X$ be a $k$-morphism, with projective line and its two standard affine charts as in [def-sc-p1-standard]. If the set-theoretic image of $r$ is a singleton $\{x\}$, then $x$ is a $k$-rational point and $r$ factors as the structural morphism $\mathbf P^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ followed by that point. Its scalar extension $r_L:\mathbf P^1_L\to X\times_kL$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] therefore has singleton image. Conversely, if $r_L$ has singleton image, so does $r$; equivalently contraction of a projective-line component is preserved and reflected by scalar extension. The converse uses surjectivity of $\mathbf P^1_L\to\mathbf P^1_k$. These assertions apply to $f|_R$ for any $k$-morphism $f:C\to X$ and any reduced closed component $R\subseteq C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_k$. No properness, separatedness, finite type or reducedness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^1_k$ and let $p:P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be its structure map. By [lem-sc-p1-monomial](i) with $d=0$, global sections of $\mathcal O(0)$ are precisely scalar multiples of the monomial $1$. In [def-sc-p1-standard], the transition for $d=0$ is $1$, so the two local generators give $\mathcal O(0)\cong\mathcal O_P$. Thus $p^\sharp:k\to\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ is an isomorphism of rings: on the two charts it sends $a$ to $(a,a)$. Explicitly, a compatible pair satisfies $u(t)=v(t^{-1})$ in $k[t,t^{-1}]$; comparing positive and negative exponents forces both polynomials to be the same constant.

source.place: Tag 01JE (example-projective-line), global-section calculation; existing monomial computation at d=0

proof.text: Choose an affine open $j:U=\operatorname{Spec}A\hookrightarrow X$ containing $x$. Since $r^{-1}(U)=P$, restriction gives $r_U:P\to U$ with $jr_U=r$: its continuous map is $r$ valued in $U$, and its sheaf map on an open $V\subseteq U$ is the original map on the same open $V\subseteq X$; local maps on stalks are unchanged [def-weil-open-immersion]. Write $\rho:A\to\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$ for $r_U^\sharp$ and $\alpha=(p^\sharp)^{-1}\rho:A\to k$. It is a $k$-algebra map because $r$ is over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], $r_U$ and $(\operatorname{Spec}\alpha)p$ are equal: both induce $\rho$. Hence $r=ap$ for the $k$-point $a=j\operatorname{Spec}\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ [def-weil-field-valued-points]. The chart $t=0$ supplies a point of $P$, so the image of $a$ is exactly $x$. This proves rationality and the required factorization.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine); restriction to an open subscheme, Tag 01HE (definition-immersion-locally-ringed-spaces)

proof.text: Base change of $r=ap$ gives $r_L=a_Lp_L$, where $a_L:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X_L$ is the pair consisting of $a$ after $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and $p_L:P_L\to\operatorname{Spec}k\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L=\operatorname{Spec}L$ is the second projection; both factorizations are the unique maps with the given projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. To identify $P_L=P\times_kL$ with $\mathbf P^1_L$, apply [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension] with $R=\mathbf Z$, $S=k$, $A=\mathbf Z[x_0,x_1]$, $B=k[x_0,x_1]$ and $\beta:k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Z[x_0,x_1]\xrightarrow{\sim}k[x_0,x_1]$ the coefficientwise isomorphism: the square of $p$, $\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is cartesian, so by uniqueness of fibre products $P\cong\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ over $k$. Associating the products then gives $P\times_kL\cong\operatorname{Spec}L\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$, which is $\mathbf P^1_L$ of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]; this isomorphism commutes with the projections to $\operatorname{Spec}L$ and to $P$, so it does not change images. Since $\operatorname{Spec}L$ has one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $r_L$ has at most one image point. The image is nonempty: the $k$-point $t=0$ of the chart $U_0$ of [def-sc-p1-standard], $z:\operatorname{Spec}k\to P$, gives the point $(z\circ(\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k),\mathrm{id})$ of $P_L$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. It is therefore a singleton.

source.place: Tag 01JP (definition-fibre-product), universal property and associativity; Tag 01JE (example-projective-line), rational point of the standard chart; base change of Proj via lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension

proof.text: Conversely, let $\pi:P_L\to P$ and $q:X_L\to X$ be the projections. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective], so its pullback $\pi$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The defining square gives $q r_L=r\pi$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $r_L(P_L)=\{y\}$, then $r(P)=r(\pi(P_L))=q(r_L(P_L))=\{q(y)\}$. This proves reflection of contraction.

source.place: Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective), applied to Spec L -> Spec k; set images in the cartesian square

proof.text: For the final assertion, choose the given $k$-isomorphism $e:P\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ and apply the preceding steps to $r=(f|_R)e$. An isomorphism is surjective, so $r(P)=(f|_R)(R)$. Its scalar extension $e_L$ is again an isomorphism: the base changes of $e$ and $e^{-1}$ compose to identities by the uniqueness clause of [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $r_L(P_L)=(f_L|_{R_L})(R_L)$, proving the same equivalence for the stated component.
